note: Adapted from Emerson's 1950 description of the new genus and species (in English), based on a single soldier holotype; the measurements are recorded as printed. The alate and worker were unknown at the time; the original compares it with the genus Psammotermes and places both in what was then the family Rhinotermitidae.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head nearly square, slightly flattened, the sides nearly parallel and slightly convex; behind the antennal fossae on each side a distinct eye spot, slightly smaller than the antennal fossa, the ommatidia degenerate and only faintly discernible; in the middle of the posterior part of the head a small glandular pore is visible; above the eye spot two pale patches, possibly degenerate ocelli. Labrum very wide, rounded at the sides, with a thin transparent margin at the tip; all tibiae with 2 spurs (2:2:2). Compared with the soldier of Psammotermes: the latter has the head and body with numerous long hairs, the mandibles more curved with coarse serrations in the middle of both, the left mandible without a basal groove, the boundary between postclypeus and frons indistinct, the labrum large and wide, without a transverse pale band, more pointed at the tip and without a transparent margin, the postmentum relatively wider at its narrowest point, the eye spot indistinct, more antennal segments, the anterior margin of the pronotum without lobes, the femora stouter, and the tibial spur formula 3:2:2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head, pronotum and abdominal tergites yellowish brown; the middle of the labrum with a broad pale transverse band. Head with a few scattered setae; postmentum with a few microscopic hairs; pronotal margins with a few setae and microscopic hairs; sides of the abdominal tergites with a few setae and microscopic hairs; labrum with 2 setae near the apical margin. Head nearly square, slightly flattened, the sides nearly parallel and slightly convex; behind the antennal fossae on each side an eye spot, slightly smaller than the antennal fossa, the ommatidia degenerate and almost indistinguishable; in the middle of the head, well behind the eye spot, a small pale glandular pore is visible; above the eye spot two pale patches, possibly degenerate ocelli, about 1/5 longer than the eye spot. Anterior part of the postmentum wide, narrowing behind, situated about 1/4—1/5 of the way in front of the middle of the posterior margin of the head; in lateral view slightly convex, with a small ridge near the neck membrane. Antennae 13-segmented, the terminal segment much narrower than the preceding one, the 3rd segment about as long as the 2nd, the 4th shorter than the 3rd. Postclypeus distinct, about 3 times as wide as long. Labrum very wide, rounded at the sides, with a thin transparent margin at the tip. Mandibles wide at the base, tapering to a sharp point, only slightly hooked; outer margin of the left mandible nearly straight, that of the right slightly curved inwards; both mandibles with a concavity about 2/9 of the distance from the base (condyle), separating a distinct basal part from an apical part; inner margin of the right mandible smooth, with a tooth-like process about 1/3 of the distance from the condyle, then rapidly narrowing; inner margin of the left mandible finely serrate behind the tip, coarser near the base, with a large basal groove to receive the tooth-like process of the right mandible; the edge below the groove coarsely serrate, above the groove smooth. Pronotum flatly arched, the anterior margin distinctly notched. Measurements (holotype, mm): head length (to the base of the mandibles) 1.56, head height 0.82, head width 1.10, postmentum width greatest 0.43 and least 0.22, postclypeus length 0.19 and width 0.57, labrum width 0.57, left mandible length 1.09, pronotal length about 0.47 and width 0.78, mesonotal length 0.41, hind tibia 1.09.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The holotype is a single soldier, collected at Itabu Creek, a tributary of the upper New River, Akarai Mountains, British Guiana (1°42′N, 57°55′W), by E. R. Blake in October 1938 (month 10), in rain forest at an elevation of about 2 000 feet. Alate and worker unknown. The locality is the same as the type localities of Labiotermes brevilabius and Labiotermes pelliceus.
